title: Sliding-window quota alignment for fragmented websocket responses
creator: Jordan Kim
description: We are seeing inconsistent quota enforcement for long-lived websocket streams that send fragmented payloads and intermittently reconnect. Customers report token usage spikes that do not match observed output, and internal audits show both double-crediting and credit leakage across sliding-window quota checks. This ticket defines the design and implementation work to align sliding-window quota accounting with fragment-level streaming semantics and reconnection behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Sliding-window quota lookups return deterministic remaining quota for a client session even when the session emits fragmented response frames across multiple connections.
No double-crediting: repeated delivery of the same fragment (from client retry or server resend) must not charge tokens twice for committed fragments.
No permanent leakage: provisional credits reserved for in-flight fragments are either committed or released within a bounded timeout and visible in the quota dashboard.
Rate-limiter integration: existing token-bucket and calendar-window rate limiters remain compatible; burst accounting reflects only committed tokens.
End-to-end tests that simulate reconnect/resume, duplicate fragments, and interleaved multiplexed streams pass in CI with synthetic metering events validated against expected token traces.
implementation_steps: Introduce fragment-level provisional credits in Metering Service: on fragment receive, reserve provisional token credits keyed by (session_id, fragment_id, resume_token).
Extend metering event schema (kafka topic metering.events) to include provisional=true/false and commit_event_id; add fragment_id and resume_token fields.
Change sliding-window calculation to treat provisional credits as pending and exclude them from enforceable remaining_quota until commit event is observed or timeout expires.
On final fragment or explicit commit from serving runtime, emit a commit event that flips provisional->committed and triggers quota deduction in the token store.
Implement dedupe on commit_event_id in the token ledger to prevent double-commit from duplicate commit events during retries.
Add a short-lived lockless tombstone record in token ledger for released provisional credits to allow eventual re-use without race conditions.

Update rate limiter adapters to query remaining_quota which now deducts only committed tokens; add fast-path that considers provisional reservations when evaluating concurrency to avoid over-accepting input that would immediately exceed quota upon commit.
Instrument and add metrics: provisional_count, provisional_bytes, provisional_age_p50/p95, committed_rate_from_provisional, provisional_timeouts.

Backfill migration: scan recent 48h provisional records and decide commit/release via heuristic (e.g., if serving runtime logs show final fragment commit) to avoid customer-impacting retroactive changes.
Ship server-side feature flag 'streaming_fragment_provisional_v1'; run in shadow mode 1 week, then opt-in for a small percentage of traffic before full rollout.
data_model_changes: kafka.meterevents schema: add fields fragment_id (string), resume_token (string), provisional (boolean), commit_event_id (string|null)
token_ledger table: add columns provisional_reservation_id, provisional_expiry_ts, commit_event_id, resume_token
add secondary index on provisional_reservation_id for fast lookup and cleanup
monitoring_and_alerting: New dashboard: Streaming Quota Health with charts for provisional vs committed tokens, provisional timeout rate, and misaligned quota denials.
Alert: provisional_timeout_rate > 0.5% over 5m -> P1 on-call -> potential leakage.
SLO: commit_lag_p95 < 30s for fragments under normal load; alert when > 2x baseline.
Audit logs: every commit/release must emit audit entry with serving node id and resume_token for post-mortem tracing.
rollout_plan: Implement feature behind 'streaming_fragment_provisional_v1' flag in Metering Service and Serving Runtime.
Run in shadow mode where provisional path records metrics but does not change enforcement for 7 days.
Enable for 1% traffic and monitor metrics for 48h.
Increase to 10% then 50% with monitoring gates; perform backfill reconciliation windows between phases.
Full enable and remove shadow mode after two release cycles and one-week stable telemetry.
test_plan: Unit tests: reservation lifecycle (reserve->commit->release), dedupe on commit_event_id, expiry cleanup.
Integration tests: simulated websocket client that sends fragmented payloads, reconnects with resume_token, and triggers duplicate fragment delivery; assert ledger shows single committed charge.
Load test: bursty multiplexed streams with provisional reservations under 2000 RPS to validate rate-limiter fast-path behavior.
Chaos test: kill serving node between fragment reserve and commit to ensure cleanup and timeout semantic correctness.
E2E CI job: run scenario matrix that compares metering.events trace to expected token deltas for 100 synthetic sessions.
notes: This approach favors safety: provisional reservations avoid undercharging when the client replays fragments, but we must bound provisional lifetime to avoid permanent leakage.
We intentionally separate provisional reservations from enforceable quota to preserve existing SLA semantics for rate limiting while preventing customer-visible 'surprise' denials.
Alternative considered: optimistic commit on first fragment accept. Rejected due to known duplicate-delivery paths from client retries and gateway retries.
Coordination needed with Console team to surface provisional metrics and explain transient 'pending' token counts in per-route dashboards.
Security: resume_token is PII-equivalent; ensure it is redacted in public logs and encrypted at rest.
